title: saveSelection() warns when no settings provider can retain the selection

source.anchor: Without a settings provider, `saveSelection()` cannot retain a selection for a later Agent.

task:
Problem: `AgentDefaultModelConfig.saveSelection()` at packages/core/agent-default-model/src/index.ts:98-104 writes through `this.ctx.get('settings')?.replace(...)`. In a composition without a settings provider the optional chain resolves successfully while nothing is stored, so the caller (packages/host/apiproxy/src/index.ts:100 forwards the web client's model choice here) reports success and the selection is lost at the next process start without any trace. The README records this only as a limitation (Known Limitations bullet quoted in the source anchor). Repository rule (AGENTS.md, 'Misconfiguration fails loud'): a missing referent is never skipped silently.

Required: a settings-less composition stays legitimate, so `saveSelection()` keeps returning normally, but when `ctx.get('settings')` is undefined it logs one warning per service instance through `this.ctx.logger.warn` that names `AGENT_DEFAULT_MODEL_SETTINGS_NAMESPACE` and states that the selection applies to this process only because no settings provider is loaded; later calls on the same instance do not repeat it. Document the behavior in the README (the `saveSelection()` description and the Known Limitations bullet, English and Chinese together), then re-record with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write packages/core/agent-default-model/README.md`. Add packages/core/agent-default-model/tests/save-selection-without-settings.spec.ts that composes the plugin without `dsh-settings`, observes the context logger, calls `saveSelection()` twice and asserts exactly one warning naming the namespace, and that a composition with the real `SettingsProvider` (the fixture of the existing spec) logs no warning.

Constraints: do not change the method's return type, the settings schema, or the apiproxy consumer.
